explanation: Splitting the bill is widely accepted in the Philippines, especially among groups of friends and even on first dates, and is commonly called "KKB" (kaniya-kaniyang bayad, "each pays their own"). However, when someone hosts or invites others out, the inviter is usually expected to pay, though guests still make a show of offering to pay. So splitting is polite in casual peer settings but can be awkward in hosted or hierarchical ones.
local_tip: With friends, say "KKB na lang" to propose splitting; if you were the one who invited or you're senior in rank, offer to cover the bill first and let others insist.

also_check.note: Splitting is common among friends, but the oldest or host often pays; arguing over the check can be rude.
Splitting is uncommon; whoever invites is expected to pay the whole bill.
It's considered polite to let companions split rather than insist on covering everything.
